insights.title: Bank credit hits a record ₹223.9L Cr, up ₹3.1L Cr
insights.body: Bank credit outstanding reached ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, the highest level in this 44-period series. Volume rose ₹3.1L Cr period-on-period (₹220.8L Cr → ₹223.9L Cr), more than July's ₹1.5L Cr addition.
insights.implication: The ₹3.1L Cr monthly addition is roughly double July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, the strongest single-month build in at least the last two periods, keeping the book at an all-time high of ₹223.9L Cr.

inferences: Bank credit outstanding hit ₹223.9L Cr in August 2026, up from ₹220.8L Cr in July — the highest level in this 44-period series.
The ₹3.1L Cr monthly addition is roughly double July's ₹1.5L Cr gain, on a book that has grown from ₹133.4L Cr in January 2023.
Bank credit has added ₹90.5L Cr since January 2023 (₹133.4L Cr → ₹223.9L Cr).

insights.title: Bank credit FY26 growth hits 16.1%, up 5.1 points from FY25
insights.body: Bank credit grew 11.0% in the year to March 2025 and 16.1% in the year to March 2026. The full-year growth rate stepped up 5.1 points, from 11.0% in FY25 to 16.1% in FY26.
insights.implication: A 5.1-point jump between full years is a large move for an annual growth measure that updates only once a year, marking a year-over-year step-up in FY26 lending versus FY25.

inferences: Bank credit grew 11.0% in FY25 and 16.1% in FY26.
That is a 5.1-point step-up between the two full years — a measure that moves only once a year, at each March close.
FY26's 16.1% is the faster of the two years by a clear margin.

insights.title: Banks deployed a record ₹29.6L Cr net new credit in FY26
insights.body: Banks deployed ₹29.6L Cr of net new credit in the full year to March 2026. This figure is unchanged at ₹29.6L Cr since it was locked at the March 2026 year-end, and sits at or near the maximum of this 44-period series.
insights.implication: Because this is a once-a-year figure fixed at the March close, its unchanged ₹29.6L Cr reading across 44 periods doesn't move with current conditions — the FY acceleration and monthly absolute signals carry that part of the story.

inferences: FY26 net new credit stands at ₹29.6L Cr, at or near the maximum reading in this 44-period series.
The figure has not moved from ₹29.6L Cr across all 44 periods because it reflects the full-year tally fixed at the March 2026 close, not a monthly flow.
It won't update again until the FY27 year-end close.

insights.title: Bank credit growth eases to 19.08% from July's 19.33% peak
insights.body: Bank credit grew 19.08% year-on-year in August 2026, down from July's 19.33%. Growth slowed 0.25 points (19.33% → 19.08%), after rising every month from April's 16.0% through July's 19.3%.
insights.implication: August's slight pullback from July's 19.33% peak is the first deceleration after three straight months of increases (16.0% in April to 19.3% in July), though at 19.08% growth remains near the highest level recorded in this window.

inferences: Bank credit grew 19.08% year-on-year in August 2026, slightly below July's 19.33%, the high point of this 26-period window.
The rate had climbed every month from April's 16.0% to July's 19.3%, before easing 0.25 points in August.
Even after the dip, August's 19.08% is still near the highest level in this 26-period window.

insights.title: Food credit falls to ₹1.12L Cr, a third straight decline
insights.body: Food credit outstanding fell to ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down ₹0.06L Cr from July's ₹1.18L Cr. Volume declined ₹0.06L Cr period-on-period (₹1.18L Cr → ₹1.12L Cr), the third consecutive monthly drop since May's all-time high of ₹1.37L Cr.
insights.implication: Three consecutive monthly declines from May's ₹1.37L Cr peak have pulled food credit down by ₹0.25L Cr (₹1.37L Cr → ₹1.12L Cr), yet the book is still reading in the upper range of this window — the pullback has not erased the earlier run-up.

inferences: Food credit stood at ₹1.12L Cr in August 2026, down from ₹1.18L Cr in July.
This is the third straight monthly decline since the ₹1.37L Cr peak in May 2026, following drops to ₹1.32L Cr in June and ₹1.18L Cr in July.
Despite three months of decline, ₹1.12L Cr remains above the upper range of this 44-period window.

insights.title: Food credit YoY growth jumps to 145.81%, a series high
insights.body: Food credit grew 145.81% year-on-year in August 2026, the highest reading in this 32-period series. Growth accelerated 37.90 points (107.91% → 145.81%), surpassing the prior high of 139.4% set in March 2026.
insights.implication: The 37.90-point jump to 145.81% is the largest year-on-year growth figure in this 32-period series, well clear of the prior high of 139.4% set in March 2026.

inferences: Food credit grew 145.81% year-on-year in August 2026, up from 107.91% in July — a 37.90-point jump.
This surpasses the previous high of 139.4% reached in March 2026, making August the strongest reading in this 32-period series.
At 145.81%, growth is now well above the lower end of this window's range (23.0%).

insights.title: Non-food credit hits a record ₹222.8L Cr, up ₹3.2L Cr
insights.body: Non-food credit outstanding reached ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, the highest level in this 44-period series. Volume rose ₹3.2L Cr period-on-period (₹219.6L Cr → ₹222.8L Cr), continuing the climb from ₹132.9L Cr in January 2023.
insights.implication: Non-food credit's ₹3.2L Cr addition in August keeps the book at a fresh all-time high of ₹222.8L Cr, extending a climb that has added ₹89.9L Cr since January 2023.

inferences: Non-food credit stood at ₹222.8L Cr in August 2026, up from ₹219.6L Cr in July — the highest level in this 44-period series.
The ₹3.2L Cr monthly addition builds on a run that has taken the book from ₹132.9L Cr in January 2023 to today's level.
Non-food credit has added ₹89.9L Cr since January 2023 (₹132.9L Cr → ₹222.8L Cr).

insights.title: Banks deployed ₹29.2L Cr net new non-food credit in FY26

insights.implication: This FY26 figure is fixed until the next annual lock in March 2027, so it won't reflect any shift until then — the monthly absolute reading is what moves in between.

inferences: FY26 non-food credit addition stands at ₹29.2L Cr, at or near the maximum reading in this 44-period series.
It has not moved from ₹29.2L Cr across all 44 periods, since this is the full-year figure locked at the March 2026 close, not a monthly flow.
This figure is fixed until the March 2027 close.

insights.title: Non-food credit eases to 18.8%, still near 26-period high
insights.body: Non-food credit grew 18.8% year-on-year in August 2026. Growth slipped from 19.1% in July to 18.8% in August, down 0.29 points.
insights.implication: This is the first easing after three straight months of acceleration, but at 18.8% growth is still running well above every level seen in this dataset outside the last few months.

inferences: Non-food credit grew 18.8% year-on-year in August 2026, down from July's 19.1%.
This ends a three-month climb that ran from 15.8% in April to 19.1% in July.
Even after the dip, 18.8% sits above the upper range of this 26-period window (where most readings fall between 10.5% and 14.8%).
The slowdown is small next to the run-up that preceded it — a 0.29-point easing after a near four-point climb since April.

insights.title: All 4 main sectors stay positive — 26th straight period
insights.body: All four main sectors — agriculture, industry, services, retail — posted positive year-on-year growth in August 2026. Breadth held at 4 of 4 sectors, unchanged from July, extending a run that began in July 2024.
insights.implication: At 26 straight periods, this is the longest stretch in the dataset where every main sector has grown together, against a record that includes a stretch in 2023 when none did.

inferences: All four main sectors show positive YoY growth in August 2026, with breadth unchanged at 4 of 4 from July.
This is the 26th consecutive period at 4 of 4, a streak that has held since Jul 2024.
Against a historical record of 38 periods, the current reading sits at or near the maximum for that window.

insights.title: Agriculture's share falls to 12.23%, tying its 2023 low
insights.body: Agriculture's share of total bank credit fell to 12.23% in Aug 2026. Share slipped 0.09pp from 12.33% in Jul 2026 to 12.23%, falling below the 25th percentile of 12.4% across 44 periods.
insights.implication: At 12.23%, agriculture's share matches its lowest point since Nov 2023 — a repeat low rather than a new one, even as the sector's own credit growth is strengthening.

inferences: Agriculture's share dropped to 12.23% in Aug 2026, down 0.09pp from 12.33% in Jul 2026.
The reading sits below the 25th percentile of 12.4% across 44 periods, in the lower range of its history.
The series has only touched this level once before, at 12.2% in Nov 2023.

insights.title: Agriculture credit growth rises to 17.22% YoY, up 0.25pp
insights.body: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% YoY in Aug 2026. Growth accelerated 0.25pp from 16.98% in Jul 2026 to 17.22%.
insights.implication: Agriculture's growth has reaccelerated to 17.22%, but that is still a middling reading for this sector — the series held at 20.0% for three straight months in early 2024, a level the current reading hasn't reached.

inferences: Agriculture credit grew 17.22% YoY in Aug 2026, up 0.25pp from 16.98% in Jul 2026.
This sits near the median of its 32-period range, between the 25th percentile of 9.5% and the 75th percentile of 17.4%.
The series ran at 20.0% for three straight months in Jan-Mar 2024, well above today's 17.22%.

insights.title: Industry FY credit growth jumps to 15.0% from 8.2%
insights.body: Industry credit grew 15.0% in the year to Mar 2026, up from 8.2% in the year to Mar 2025. Full-year growth stepped up 6.8 points, from 8.2% in FY25 to 15.0% in FY26.
insights.implication: This is an annual measure, fixed only at the Mar 2026 year-end: industry credit's annual growth nearly doubled between FY25 and FY26, from 8.2% to 15.0%.

inferences: Industry credit grew 8.2% in the year to Mar 2025 and 15.0% in the year to Mar 2026.
That is a 6.8-point step-up in annual growth, set once at the Mar 2026 year-end.
FY26's 15.0% rate is nearly double FY25's 8.2%.

insights.title: Industry's share drops to 21.53%, matching its 2026 low
insights.body: Industry's share of total bank credit stood at 21.53% in Aug 2026. Share fell 0.33pp from 21.86% in Jul 2026 to 21.53%, below the 25th percentile of 21.7%.
insights.implication: Industry's 21.53% share matches the 21.5% floor already seen four times in 2026, making Aug a repeat low rather than a new one.

inferences: Industry's share fell to 21.53% in Aug 2026, down 0.33pp from 21.86% in Jul 2026.
The reading is below the 25th percentile of 21.7% across 44 periods, in the lower range of its history.
The series already touched 21.5% four times in 2026 — Jan, Feb, Mar and Apr.

insights.title: Industry credit growth slows to 18.23% YoY after 20% peak
insights.body: Industry credit grew 18.23% YoY in Aug 2026. Growth decelerated 1.72pp from 19.95% in Jul 2026 to 18.23% — the first pullback since the climb from May 2025's 5.3% low.
insights.implication: This is industry credit's first deceleration since the run from a 5.3% low in May 2025 to a 20.0% peak in Jul 2026 — the pullback to 18.23% stays above the 75th percentile of 13.9%, reading as a pause near the highs rather than a reversal.

inferences: Industry credit grew 18.23% YoY in Aug 2026, down 1.72pp from 19.95% in Jul 2026.
That follows a climb from a 5.3% low in May 2025 to a 20.0% peak in Jul 2026.
Even after the pullback, 18.23% stays above the 75th percentile of 13.9% across this 26-period window.

insights.title: Personal Loans is the biggest slice of the parent category at 32.7%
insights.body: Personal Loans holds the largest share of the parent category at 32.7%, Services 28.3%; Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.2%. These are size shares, not growth rates. Top three hold 82.5% of the parent category, spread 20.5 percentage points.
insights.implication: Composition, not momentum: Personal Loans carries the most weight of the parent category. Concentration means the big blocks drive the category — watch them first.

inferences: Personal Loans is the largest block at 32.7% of the parent category.
Agriculture and Allied Activities is the smallest at 12.2% — a 20.5 percentage points spread across 4 sub-categories.
The top three hold 82.5% of the parent category — concentrated mix.

insights.title: Services growing fastest at 24.3%; Personal Loans slowest at 16.9%
insights.body: Services leads YoY growth at 24.3%, Industry at 18.2%; Personal Loans is slowest at 16.9%. 4 of 4 categories growing, spread 7.4 percentage points.
insights.implication: Services is the fastest at 24.3% and the largest block at 28.1% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Services is the standout at 24.3% YoY.
Personal Loans is the weakest at 16.9% — a spread of 7.4 percentage points across 4 categories.
4 of 4 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Personal loans hold steady at 32.71% share of total credit
insights.body: Personal loans held 32.71% of total bank credit in Aug 2026. Share was unchanged from last period at 32.71%, within the 32.4%–32.9% range seen over the past 44 periods.
insights.implication: Personal loans' share of total credit has gone flat at 32.71% for a second straight period, sitting mid-range rather than extending the prior period's small gain.

inferences: Personal loans' share stayed at 32.71% in Aug 2026, identical to the prior period's 32.71%.
That reading sits near the median of its 44-period range (32.4% to 32.9%), not at either extreme.
The share has now gone flat after edging up 0.07 points the period before.

insights.title: Personal loans growth jumps to 16.92% YoY — a new high
insights.body: Personal loans credit grew 16.92% year-on-year in Aug 2026. Growth accelerated from 16.23% to 16.92%, a 0.69-point gain, now at or near the highest level in this 26-period series.
insights.implication: Personal loans growth has set a new high at 16.92%, extending the run that began when growth bottomed near 11.1% in May 2025 — the sector has now outgrown every other reading in this 26-period series.

inferences: Personal loans grew 16.92% YoY in Aug 2026, up 0.69 points from 16.23% last period.
That is at or near the highest reading across all 26 periods, above the 11.9%–15.3% range covering most of the window.
Growth has climbed from 11.1% in May 2025 through 16.2% in Jul 2026 to 16.92% now, each recent period setting a fresh high.

insights.title: Services credit accelerated 7.0 points in FY26 to 19.0%
insights.body: Services credit grew 19.0% in the year to Mar 2026, up from 12.0% in the year to Mar 2025. Full-year growth stepped up from 12.0% in FY25 to 19.0% in FY26, a 7.0-point acceleration measured at the Mar 2026 year-end.
insights.implication: Services credit's full-year growth rate stepped up by 7.0 points between FY25 and FY26 (12.0% to 19.0%), a reading fixed at the March year-end.

inferences: Services credit grew 12.0% in the year to Mar 2025 and 19.0% in the year to Mar 2026.
The 7.0-point gap between those two annual rates is this signal's full-year acceleration reading.
This is an annual reading set once a year at March year-end, not a monthly trend.

insights.title: Services credit share rises to 28.27%, above its usual range
insights.body: Services accounted for 28.27% of total bank credit in Aug 2026. Share rose from 28.22% to 28.27%, a 0.05-point gain, sitting above the 27.3%–27.8% range that covers most of this 44-period series.
insights.implication: Services' share resumed climbing to 28.27% after last period's near-flat reading, staying above 28% for six straight months since the Mar 2026 peak of 28.5%.

inferences: Services credit's share rose to 28.27% in Aug 2026, up 0.05 points from 28.22% last period.
That is above the 27.3%-to-27.8% band covering most of the 44-period series, in the upper range.
The share has stayed at or above 28% every month since the Mar 2026 peak of 28.5% — six readings in a row.

insights.title: Services credit growth accelerates to 24.35%, near-record high
insights.body: Services credit grew 24.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 22.94% in Jul 2026. Growth climbed from 22.94% in Jul 2026 to 24.35% in Aug 2026, a 1.40-point gain, continuing an unbroken rise from 18.6% in Apr 2026.
insights.implication: Services credit has now accelerated for four straight months since the April dip to 18.6%, reaching 24.35% — at or near the highest reading in this 26-period series, with no sign yet of levelling off.

inferences: Services credit grew 24.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026, accelerating 1.40 points from 22.94% in Jul 2026.
This is the fourth consecutive monthly acceleration since April 2026's dip to 18.6%, with growth rising to 20.4% in May, 21.4% in Jun, 22.94% in Jul and now 24.35%.
At 24.35%, services credit growth is at or near its highest level in this 26-period dataset, well above the 11.2%-16.8% range that covered most of the window.

insights.title: Services took 35.0% of all new bank credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the bank credit added over the past twelve months, Services took 35.0% — the largest share of the new money — growing 24.3% a year and accelerating (+1.40 pp). The rest went to Personal Loans 30.0%; Industry 21.0%; Agriculture and Allied Activities 11.4%. Industry took 21.0% while growing 18.2% a year and slowing (-1.72 pp) — a smaller slice of a faster-growing total, not a retreat.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's bank credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Services accounts for 35.0% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.

insights.title: Medium growing fastest at 31.8%; Large slowest at 14.9%
insights.body: Medium leads YoY growth at 31.8%, Micro and Small at 23.0%; Large is slowest at 14.9%. 3 of 3 categories growing, spread 16.9 percentage points.
insights.implication: Medium is the fastest at 31.8% and the largest block at 2.2% of the category — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Medium is the standout at 31.8% YoY.
Large is the weakest at 14.9% — a spread of 16.9 percentage points across 3 categories.
3 of 3 categories are growing — broad-based momentum.

insights.title: Large corporate share falls to 66.55%, lowest in 44 periods
insights.body: Large corporates held 66.55% of industry credit, down from 67.26% the prior period. Share fell from 67.26% to 66.55%, a 0.71-point drop that breaks the 67.2%-67.4% band the share had held for the prior five periods.
insights.implication: The 0.71-point fall ends a five-period plateau and pushes large corporates' share of industry credit to a new low for this series, even as large-corporate credit itself keeps growing fast — the rest of the industry book is gaining ground faster.

inferences: Large corporate share dropped to 66.55%, down 0.71 points from 67.26% last period.
That drop breaks the 67.2%-67.4% band the share had held for five straight periods before this one.
At 66.55%, the share is now at or near the lowest point in this 44-period series, below the typical range this signal has held, which bottoms near 68.1%.

insights.title: Large corporate credit growth cools to 14.9% from 17.7% peak
insights.body: Large corporate credit grew 14.88% YoY, decelerating from 17.69% the prior period. Growth slowed from 17.69% to 14.88%, a 2.81-point deceleration that breaks the seven-period acceleration run from 5.5% in Jan 2026 to 17.7% in Jul 2026.
insights.implication: The 2.81-point pullback marks the first deceleration after seven straight periods of acceleration, but at 14.88% growth is still well above its typical range, which tops out near 8.5% — a cooling, not a reversal.

inferences: Large corporate credit grew 14.88% YoY, down 2.81 points from 17.69% last period.
This ends the seven-period run of acceleration that had taken growth from 5.5% in Jan 2026 to a peak of 17.69%.
Even after the pullback, 14.88% is still above the typical high end of this series, which tops out near 8.5%, among the strongest readings in this 32-period series.

insights.title: Medium enterprises' industry credit share hits 10.2%, a new high
insights.body: Medium enterprises account for 10.19% of industry credit in Aug 2026, the highest share in this 44-period window. Share rose from 10.0% last period to 10.2%, extending past the Jul 2026 peak. The recent trajectory is 9.7% → 9.7% → 9.9% → 10.0% → 10.2%.
insights.implication: Medium enterprises have added to their industry-credit share for a second straight period after breaking 10% in Jul 2026, taking the share to a fresh high of 10.2% against a historical p75 of just 9.4%.

inferences: Medium enterprises' share of industry credit rose to 10.19% in Aug 2026, up 0.20pp from 9.99% last period.
That is the highest reading in the 44-period series, above the prior range's p75 of 9.4%.
The gain extends a climb that has run from 8.0% in Jan 2023 to 10.2% now, with no period yet pulling the share back down.

insights.title: Medium enterprise credit growth hits 31.8% YoY, a fresh high
insights.body: Medium enterprise credit grew 31.78% YoY in Aug 2026, the fastest pace in this 32-period window. Growth rose from 30.48% last period to 31.78%, up 1.30pp, extending above Jul 2026's 30.5% and Jun 2026's 30.3%.
insights.implication: Medium enterprise growth has now held above 30% for three consecutive periods and is still climbing, at 31.78% against a historical p75 of just 20.5% for this line.

inferences: Medium enterprise credit growth reached 31.78% in Aug 2026, up 1.30pp from 30.48% in Jul 2026.
That is the third straight period above 30%, following 30.3% in Jun 2026 and 30.5% in Jul 2026, and sits at or near the maximum of the 32-period series (p75 of 20.5%).
The pace has roughly tripled since Jun 2025's 13.2%, the low point of the series.

insights.title: Micro & Small credit accelerated 23.8 points to 32.7% in FY26
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprise credit grew 8.9% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 32.7% in the year ending Mar 2026, a 23.8 percentage point acceleration. Full-year growth stepped up from 8.9% in FY25 to 32.7% in FY26, a 23.8-point move. This is an annual figure set at the March year-end; it does not change month to month.
insights.implication: The 23.8pp jump between FY25's 8.9% and FY26's 32.7% is the sharpest full-year step-up in this dataset for Micro & Small credit.

inferences: Micro & Small credit grew 8.9% in FY25 and 32.7% in FY26 — a 23.8pp step-up between the two full years.
The metric is fixed at each March year-end, so the FY26 rate of 32.7% reflects the full year, not a single month's reading.
This is the widest FY-over-FY step-up recorded for this line in the dataset.

insights.title: Micro & Small share jumps to 23.3%, nearing Jan's 23.5% peak
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprises account for 23.26% of industry credit in Aug 2026, up 0.51pp from the prior period. Share rose from 22.75% last period to 23.26%, reversing the Jun–Jul plateau around 22.7%–22.8% and moving to within 0.2pp of the series' highest reading of 23.5% in Jan 2026.
insights.implication: After two periods stalled near 22.7%–22.8%, Micro & Small's share jumped 0.51pp to 23.26%, closing back in on the Jan 2026 high of 23.5% without yet reaching it.

inferences: Micro & Small's industry credit share rose 0.51pp to 23.26% in Aug 2026, up from 22.75% in Jul 2026.
That reverses the two-period stall at 22.7%–22.8% seen in Jun and Jul 2026.
The current 23.26% sits just below the series' peak of 23.5% reached in Jan 2026, and above the historical p75 of 22.5%.

insights.title: Micro & Small growth ticks up to 23.0%, ending a 4-period slide
insights.body: Micro & Small enterprise credit grew 22.96% YoY in Aug 2026, up 0.40pp from the prior period. Growth rose from 22.56% last period to 22.96%, breaking the deceleration that had run from a 32.7% peak in Mar 2026 down to 22.56% in Jul 2026.
insights.implication: The uptick to 22.96% breaks a run of declines from the Mar 2026 peak of 32.7%, though growth remains well below that peak and near the series' median.

inferences: Micro & Small growth rose 0.40pp to 22.96% in Aug 2026, up from 22.56% in Jul 2026.
That ends a run of declines from the Mar 2026 peak of 32.7% through May 2026's 26.2%, Jun 2026's 23.0% and Jul 2026's 22.56%.
The 22.96% reading sits near the historical median, between the p25 of 12.4% and p75 of 24.2%.

insights.implication: After narrowing for three straight periods to its tightest gap of 4.9pp in Jul 2026, the spread widened back out to 8.1pp in Aug 2026.

inferences: The MSME vs large corporate growth spread widened 3.2pp to 8.1pp in Aug 2026, up from 4.9pp in Jul 2026.

The 8.1pp reading sits near the median of the 32-period series, well below the Jan 2026 peak of 25.7pp.

insights.implication: Agriculture growth has stopped moving in either direction — the 0.04-point change is the smallest in the recent series — and it is holding near the top of its 32-period range rather than mid-pack.

inferences: PSL Agriculture grew 19.44% in Aug 2026, barely changed from 19.40% in Jul 2026 (+0.04 points).
That reading sits above the 32-period p75 of 17.8%, in the upper range of the series.
The segment has now spent three consecutive months between 19.4% and 19.9%, after climbing from 6.1% in Jun 2025.

insights.title: PSL Educational Loans ease to 15.91% YoY, down 0.80 points
insights.body: PSL Educational Loans grew 15.91% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 16.70% in Jul 2026. Growth slowed 0.80 points, continuing a decline from 22.3% in Jun 2026, and now sits near the median of its 32-period range (p25=2.7%, p75=18.2%).
insights.implication: Educational Loans growth has now fallen for two straight months since its 22%+ run through Jun 2026, moving from the upper range back toward the middle of its historical distribution.

inferences: Educational Loans grew 15.91% in Aug 2026, down 0.80 points from 16.70% in Jul 2026.
That extends a slide from 22.3% in Jun 2026, a two-month drop of roughly 6.4 points.
The current 15.91% reading sits near the median of the 32-period range (p25=2.7%, p75=18.2%), well below the 24.0% peak reached in Feb 2026.

insights.title: PSL Housing growth falls to 9.55% YoY, a third straight drop
insights.body: PSL Housing credit grew 9.55% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 10.61% in Jul 2026. Growth eased a further 1.06 points, extending a slide from 21.3% in Jun 2026 and 39.0% in May 2026, now near the median of its 26-period range (p25=0.1%, p75=33.7%).
insights.implication: Housing has declined for three straight months from a near-40% peak to under 10%, the longest consecutive slide in this segment's 26-period series.

inferences: Housing grew 9.55% in Aug 2026, down 1.06 points from 10.61% in Jul 2026.
This is the third consecutive monthly decline, following drops from 39.0% in May 2026 to 21.3% in Jun 2026 to 10.61% in Jul 2026.
The segment has fallen below 10%, after sitting near its 26-period p75 of 33.7% as recently as Apr-May 2026.

insights.title: PSL Medium Enterprises hit a new high at 31.01% YoY
insights.body: PSL Medium Enterprises credit grew 31.01% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 29.20% in Jul 2026. Growth accelerated 1.81 points, from 29.2% to 31.0%, marking a third consecutive series high after 27.5% in Jun 2026.
insights.implication: Medium Enterprises have set a new series high for three consecutive months, each faster than the last, with no sign yet of the acceleration leveling off.

inferences: Medium Enterprises grew 31.01% in Aug 2026, up 1.81 points from 29.20% in Jul 2026.
That extends back-to-back series highs: 27.5% in Jun 2026, 29.2% in Jul 2026, now 31.0% in Aug 2026.
The reading sits at or near the maximum of the 32-period range (p25=16.4%, p75=21.4%), well above its own p75.

insights.title: PSL MSME FY26 growth hits 29.4%, up 15.9 points from FY25
insights.body: PSL Micro & Small enterprises credit grew 13.4% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 29.4% in the year ending Mar 2026 — a 15.9-point acceleration. Full-year growth stepped up from 13.4% → 29.4% between FY25 and FY26, a 15.9-point acceleration.
insights.implication: The 15.9-point full-year step-up, from 13.4% in FY25 to 29.4% in FY26, marks a sustained shift in annual credit deployment toward Micro & Small enterprises rather than a one-off reading.

inferences: PSL Micro & Small enterprises credit grew 13.4% in the year ending Mar 2025 and 29.4% in the year ending Mar 2026 — a 15.9-point acceleration.
The 15.9-point step-up reflects a sustained one-year shift in annual credit deployment to this segment, not a single month's move.
Full-year growth for the segment stands more than twice as high in FY26 (29.4%) as it was in FY25 (13.4%).

insights.title: PSL Micro & Small credit growth ticks up to 25.95%, ends plateau
insights.body: PSL Micro & Small enterprises credit grew 25.95% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 24.06% in Jul 2026. Growth accelerated by 1.89 points, from 24.1% → 25.9%, moving back above the 24.5% upper mark for this 32-period series.
insights.implication: The 1.89-point move to 25.95% breaks the narrow band of 23.7%–24.5% the segment had held for three straight months, pushing growth back above the 24.5% upper range for this 32-period series.

inferences: PSL Micro & Small enterprises credit grew 25.95% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up 1.89 points from 24.06% in Jul 2026.
That lifts the reading above the 24.5% upper range for this 32-period series, after readings of 23.7%, 24.5% and 24.1% in the three prior months.
The move breaks a run of readings clustered near 24% across May, Jun and Jul 2026.

insights.title: PSL Renewable Energy hits 32-period positive YoY streak, a record
insights.body: PSL Renewable Energy has posted positive year-on-year growth for 32 consecutive periods, through Aug 2026. The streak extended from 31 periods in Jul 2026 to 32 now, unbroken since the series began in Jan 2024.
insights.implication: PSL Renewable Energy has not recorded a single negative year-on-year reading across all 32 periods measured — the longest run available in this series.

inferences: PSL Renewable Energy has grown year-on-year for 32 consecutive periods through Aug 2026, up from 31 in Jul 2026.
The streak has not reset once across the full 32-period series tracked since Jan 2024.
Every period measured for this segment has shown positive year-on-year growth.

insights.title: PSL Renewable Energy growth cools to 25.96%, down 5.74 points
insights.body: PSL Renewable Energy credit grew 25.96% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 31.70% in Jul 2026. Growth decelerated by 5.74 points, from 31.7% → 26.0%, reversing last period's jump from 20.2% in Jun 2026.
insights.implication: The deceleration to 25.96% reverses last period's jump from 20.2% and brings growth back near the lower part of its 32-period range of 25.5% to 74.7%.

inferences: PSL Renewable Energy grew 25.96% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down 5.74 points from 31.70% in Jul 2026.
That reverses the acceleration seen in Jul 2026, when growth had jumped from 20.2% in Jun 2026.
The reading now sits closer to the 25.5%–74.7% band that has bounded this 32-period series.

insights.title: PSL Social Infrastructure rebounds to 41.49% YoY after two-period slide
insights.body: PSL Social Infrastructure credit grew 41.49% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up from 36.76% in Jul 2026. Growth accelerated by 4.74 points, from 36.8% → 41.5%, breaking the two-period slide from the 70.7% peak in May 2026.
insights.implication: The rebound to 41.49% halts the slide from May 2026's 70.7% peak and puts growth back above the 34.9% upper range for this historically volatile segment.

inferences: PSL Social Infrastructure grew 41.49% year-on-year in Aug 2026, up 4.74 points from 36.76% in Jul 2026.
That ends two straight periods of deceleration that had taken growth down from a 70.7% peak in May 2026 to 36.76% in Jul 2026.
The reading is now above the 34.9% upper range for this 32-period series.

insights.title: PSL Weaker Sections growth slips to 14.7%, third month lower
insights.body: PSL Weaker Sections (including PSLC SF/MF) grew 14.73% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 15.18% in Jul 2026. Growth fell 0.45 points, continuing a slide from 15.3% in Jun 2026 → 15.2% in Jul 2026 → 14.7% in Aug 2026.
insights.implication: The 0.45-point fall in Aug 2026 is a sharper step down than the 0.11-point dip seen going into Jul 2026, so the earlier read of this segment as flat near its strongest level no longer holds with three consecutive monthly declines.

inferences: Weaker Sections growth fell to 14.73% in Aug 2026 from 15.18% in Jul 2026, a 0.45-point drop.
That is the third straight month lower, following 15.3% in Jun 2026 and 15.2% in Jul 2026.
The reading now sits near the middle of its range across this 26-period window, not at either edge.

insights.title: PSL Weaker Sections YoY down to 14.7%, third straight fall
insights.body: PSL Weaker Sections grew 14.73% year-on-year in Aug 2026, down from 15.18% in Jul 2026. Growth slid 0.45 points, from 15.2% in Jul 2026 to 14.7% in Aug 2026, extending a decline from 15.3% in Jun 2026.
insights.implication: The pace of the slowdown has picked up — Aug 2026's 0.45-point drop is larger than the prior month's 0.11-point dip — turning what had looked like a flat reading into a three-month decline.

inferences: Weaker Sections growth is 14.73% in Aug 2026, down 0.45 points from 15.18% in Jul 2026.

Against a 26-period range where p25 and p75 bracket the series, the current reading sits near the middle rather than near its recent high.

insights.title: Social Infrastructure growing fastest at 41.5%; Export Credit slowest at -9.7%

insights.implication: Social Infrastructure is the fastest at 41.5%; Export Credit the slowest at -9.7%. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Social Infrastructure is the standout at 41.5% YoY.

insights.title: Others shed ground to Micro and Small Enterprises — the net barely moved
insights.body: Priority sector credit shows almost no net change over the year, but a great deal happened underneath it: Micro and Small Enterprises expanded while Others contracted by a similar amount. Micro and Small Enterprises accounts for 39.0% of the total movement and Others for -0.1%. Almost none of that movement survives into the net figure — this period is a transfer between members, not a change in size.
insights.implication: The headline number is the least informative part of this period. The reallocation between members is the finding.

inferences: Each sector's change over the year is measured, then compared with the total movement ignoring direction.
Coherence — the net change divided by the total movement ignoring direction — is near zero here, meaning gains and losses very nearly cancel.
At this level a share of the NET change is not meaningful, so the reading is the transfer between members.

gaps.title: PSL Export Credit deepens to -9.73% YoY, down 0.90 points
gaps.body: PSL Export Credit contracted 9.73% year-on-year in Aug 2026, worse than the -8.84% contraction in Jul 2026. The contraction deepened by 0.90 points, from -8.84% to -9.73%, reversing the improvement seen in Jul 2026.
gaps.implication: Export Credit's contraction widened again after one period of improvement, meaning the Jul 2026 recovery did not hold into Aug.

inferences: Export Credit contracted 9.73% in Aug 2026, compared with -8.84% in Jul 2026, a 0.90-point deepening.
Jul 2026 had marked an improvement from -10.74% in Jun 2026, so Aug's move reverses that direction.
The current -9.73% reading sits near the median of the 32-period range (p25=-13.3%, p75=5.2%), still well short of positive growth.

gaps.title: PSL Others reverses to -3.35% YoY, ending 4-period improvement streak
gaps.body: PSL Others contracted 3.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026, compared with a 1.12% contraction in Jul 2026. The contraction widened by 2.23 points, from -1.1% → -3.3%, after easing steadily from -12.5% in Apr 2026 through four straight months.
gaps.implication: After four consecutive periods of easing from -12.5% in Apr 2026 to -1.12% in Jul 2026, the contraction widened again to -3.35%, breaking that improving run.

inferences: PSL Others fell 3.35% year-on-year in Aug 2026, worse than the 1.12% contraction recorded in Jul 2026.
That ends four consecutive periods of easing that had taken the contraction from -12.5% in Apr 2026 to -1.12% in Jul 2026.
The segment remains between the -23.6% and 2.8% band that has bounded this 32-period series.

insights.body: RBI breaks basic-metals credit into two sub-categories. Iron and Steel holds 69.2% and Other Metal and Metal Product 30.8% — these are size shares, not growth rates. Together the two break-outs cover 100.0% of basic-metals credit — the full category.
insights.implication: Read this as size mix, not momentum: Iron and Steel is clearly the bigger block. Check the matching growth scan before positioning.

inferences: Iron and Steel is the larger break-out at 69.2% of basic-metals credit.
Other Metal and Metal Product holds 30.8% — a 38.5 percentage points gap between the only two break-outs.
Together they cover 100.0% of basic-metals credit — the full category.

insights.implication: Iron and Steel is the fastest at 21.5% and the largest block at 69.2% of basic-metals credit — pace and weight point the same way. Most of the category is growing.

inferences: Iron and Steel is the faster of the two at 21.5% YoY.

Both are growing — the gap is about pace, not direction.

inferences: Edible Oils and Vanaspati is the standout at 46.0% YoY.

insights.title: Industry credit mix rotating toward All Engineering (+0.82 pp share in a year)
insights.body: Compared with the same month a year ago, the biggest share gains in industry credit came from All Engineering +0.82 pp; Vehicles, Vehicle Parts and Transport Equipment +0.42 pp; Gems and Jewellery +0.41 pp. The ground came from Infrastructure -2.32 pp; Petroleum, Coal Products and Nuclear Fuels -0.12 pp; Textiles -0.09 pp. In all, 2.76 pp of the mix changed hands. The cessions concentrate in energy & logistics capex; the gains span several parts of the economy.
insights.implication: This is a composition read: it says where the mix is shifting, not why and not what happens next. With no single theme behind the movers, treat each segment's shift on its own terms rather than as one story.

inferences: Each segment's share of industry credit is compared with the same month a year earlier — the change is in percentage points of the mix.
Top gainer: All Engineering at +0.82 pp. Biggest cession: Infrastructure at -2.32 pp.
Rotation mass — the share that changed hands — is 2.76 pp.
The cessions concentrate in energy & logistics capex; the gains span several parts of the economy.

insights.title: Infrastructure took 19.0% of all new industry credit in the past year
insights.body: Of the industry credit added over the past twelve months, Infrastructure took 19.0% — the largest share of the new money — growing 10.2% a year and steady (-0.04 pp). The rest went to All Engineering 11.7%; Basic Metal and Metal Product 11.5%; Other Industries (not broken down) 9.6%; Chemicals and Chemical Products 8.7%; Food Processing 6.2%; Textiles 6.1%; Vehicles, Vehicle Parts and Transport Equipment 5.8%; Construction 5.3%; Gems and Jewellery 5.0%; Petroleum, Coal Products and Nuclear Fuels 3.5%; Rubber, Plastic and their Products 2.4%; Mining and Quarrying 1.3%; Cement and Cement Products 1.2%; Paper and Paper Products 1.1%; Wood and Wood Products 0.7%; Glass and Glassware 0.5%; Beverage and Tobacco 0.4%; Leather and Leather Products 0.2%. Petroleum, Coal Products and Nuclear Fuels took 3.5% while growing 14.8% a year and slowing (-19.20 pp) — a smaller slice of a faster-growing total, not a retreat.
insights.implication: Shares of new lending move far faster than shares of the book, so this is the earlier read of the two. It says where the money went, not why — and a falling share alongside rising growth means the others grew faster, not that this one shrank.

inferences: Every sector's industry credit is compared with the same month a year earlier, and each one's share of the total increase is taken.
Infrastructure accounts for 19.0% of the increase.
All sectors moved the same way this window, so the shares of the net increase are bounded and sum to a hundred.

insights.title: Infrastructure credit grew, but Telecommunications and Railways moved against it
insights.body: Infrastructure credit rose over the past year, but not everywhere: Telecommunications and Railways contracted while the rest expanded. Power accounts for 82.7% of all the movement in the period. Because parts moved in opposite directions, much of the movement cancels out and the net figure understates how much actually shifted.
insights.implication: A growing total with members moving the other way is a different claim from broad growth. Read the members, not the headline.

inferences: Each sector's change over the year is measured, then compared with the total movement ignoring direction.
Coherence — the net change divided by the total movement ignoring direction — measures whether the parts agree.
Below one, some sectors are cancelling others out, so shares of the NET change would overstate; shares of total movement are reported instead.

gaps.title: Infrastructure credit growth holds at 10.18% YoY
gaps.body: Infrastructure credit grew 10.18% YoY in Aug 2026. Growth was flat, down just 0.04pp from 10.23% in Jul 2026 to 10.18%, just under May 2026's 11.6% peak.
gaps.implication: Infrastructure credit growth has plateaued just under its 11.6% May 2026 peak, holding above the 75th percentile of 8.6% — a sharp turnaround from the -1.3% contraction recorded in May 2025.

inferences: Infrastructure credit grew 10.18% YoY in Aug 2026, almost unchanged from 10.23% in Jul 2026.
That keeps growth above the 75th percentile of 8.6% across 32 periods, in the upper range of its history.
It remains below the series peak of 11.6% hit in May 2026, after a -1.3% contraction in May 2025.
